card.band: 8 h. A frontier agent usually lands basic rendering but misses manifest semantics, conditionals, git templates and workspace edge cases. Buckets: local templates, variables, git source, conditionals, hooks, workspace. A weaker model stalls on the Rust build and the CLI plumbing.
card.cheat: Hard-coding outputs for the visible templates. The hidden templates are generated and unseen, and the check is on file trees, not on source.
card.grading: Hidden CLI behavioural tests build template trees from a generator, run the new command and compare the resulting file tree byte for byte against expected trees. The existing offline-capable uv tests act as a regression gate. Reward is the fraction of hidden cases passed over those the reference passes. A visible sample of 40 cases is included.
card.reference: Written by us: about 2500 lines of Rust across the CLI, a template engine, git fetch, and tests. It passes all hidden cases. The upstream issue was never implemented, so there is no merged answer to recall.
card.task: /app ships a history-less snapshot of uv at the base commit with a prebuilt offline cargo vendor dir. The agent adds template-driven project creation: local-directory and file:// git templates, variable prompts and defaults supplied by flags and a template manifest, file and path rendering, conditional files, post-create steps, and lockfile and workspace integration. Delivered through the uv CLI.

spike_plan.kill_if: Curated offline subset cannot be made deterministic, or the generator's expected trees cannot be reproduced from the spec alone.
spike_plan.pass_if: Offline build and curated subset are green and repeatable; generator output is deterministic; a stub passes local-copy cases while manifest, git and conditional buckets fail, giving graded partial credit.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, clone uv at 2b50cbc and run the cargo offline build with --locked to confirm the 249 s build from the probe.
Pick a curated list of offline-capable nextest tests (exclude network and flaky tests) and confirm the list runs green in under 20 min on three repeat runs.
Write a short template spec (manifest keys, variable syntax, rendering rules) and a 40-case generator with expected trees.
Stub a minimal local-directory template copy (no manifest, no git) inside the build and check that it passes the subset of cases that needs only local copying, to confirm the grader discriminates.
Check determinism: rerun the generator and grader three times with the same seed and confirm identical expected trees and scores.
Measure how far a stub gets on each bucket to confirm partial credit is steady, not all-or-nothing.

v1.summary: Seed S-im-007 passes validation with no kill: the uv issue is real, open and unimplemented, the 0.13.4 release exists, and licence is Apache-2.0. Main risks are the full test suite being unusable as a gate (amber, timeouts, non-deterministic) and that the template spec must be written precisely, since byte-exact tree comparison depends on it.

v2.note: Issue #9754 is real, open and unimplemented. But the manifest format, variable syntax and rendering rules would all be written by us, so the paper trail covers the request only, not the spec. Byte-for-byte tree comparison would accept another valid solution only if the task text pins every rendering rule, and that is not shown yet. The reference is not written. The full nextest suite timed out in all three runs and was not deterministic, so the regression gate must be a curated subset that has not been verified. pytest-cases at 0.16 is just over the novelty line. The build estimate of about 3 days is optimistic. Keep it only if the spike shows a fully pinned spec and a deterministic curated gate.
